title: Gideon in the winepress (Judges 6:11–16)
hook: hiding while threshing wheat, the least of his family is called mighty man of valor

segments.voice: Yesterday, Deborah under the palm, prophet and judge. Your line was a mother in israel.

A man is threshing wheat in a winepress. That's an odd place for it. A winepress is a pit for treading grapes, and he's down inside it, beating out grain where nobody passing by can see. The text gives the reason: "to hide it from the Midianites." Raiders have been sweeping in when the crops come up, and Israel has taken to dens and caves in the mountains. His name is Gideon. While he crouches in that pit, the angel of the LORD sits down under an oak nearby and greets him with words that, in that moment, sound almost absurd.

In the King James Bible: "The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour." To a man hiding in a hole. Gideon doesn't take the compliment. He argues, and his first argument is about God, not himself: "Oh my Lord, if the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us?" Where, he asks, are the miracles our fathers told us about? It's a raw question, and the text lets it stand. What he gets back isn't an explanation. It's a job: "Go in this thy might, and thou shalt save Israel from the hand of the Midianites: have not I sent thee?" What might? So Gideon tries a second argument, about himself: "Oh my Lord, wherewith shall I save Israel? behold, my family is poor in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father's house." He's telling the truth as he sees it. And the reply doesn't argue. It doesn't say you're stronger than you think. It says: "Surely I will be with thee." Here's the turn. The name comes first. Gideon is called mighty man of valor before he has done one brave thing. Some readers hear God seeing what Gideon will become. Others hear a name he can grow into only because God goes with him. Either way, the word arrives before the evidence. And Gideon still isn't convinced. He asks for a sign, and later for more: a fleece left out overnight, wet and then dry. The Bible doesn't hide his doubting. It keeps him in the story anyway.
screen: `MIGHTY MAN OF VALOR, IN A HOLE.`
`WHY THEN IS ALL THIS BEFALLEN US?`
`I AM THE LEAST IN MY FATHER'S HOUSE.`

segments.voice: Bring back something kind someone once said about you that you waved away: you're a good friend, you're brave, you're good at this. Notice what rises up to argue with it, the way Gideon argued, and don't argue back or force yourself to agree; just let the words stay in the room while you breathe. If you pray, let God hear the argument too, as Gideon did.
Gideon. The man hiding grain in a winepress, called mighty man of valor before he had done anything brave.
Your line: you, mighty? In this story, the name comes before the courage. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Some Christians turn to Gideon's call when they feel too small for a task, and some preachers use the greeting 'mighty man of valour' to speak about God naming people for what they can become.

fork.setup: you're Gideon, hiding in a winepress. a stranger says: the LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valor. what do you say?

original.note: Hebrew: mighty man of valor, the angel's greeting to Gideon in Judges 6:12.

trapdoor: what you thought: Gideon was a great warrior.
what it means: Gideon was hiding when he was called mighty. the name came before the courage.
what a scholar hears: gibbor hechayil, spoken in 6:12 to a man in a winepress, and answered in 6:16 with a promise, not an explanation.

chat.says: Why would God call Gideon a 'mighty man of valor' while he was hiding?
options: The name comes first: he's called mighty before he's done anything brave.
Gideon had already won battles, so the title was just stating the facts.
It was a family title passed down from his father, not about Gideon.
chat.meaning: Gideon is called mighty man of valor before he does one brave thing, and the promise is company: surely I will be with thee.

winepress.meaning: a pit for treading grapes, where Gideon hid his threshing

Midianites.meaning: raiders who stripped Israel's land when the crops came up

Manasseh.meaning: Gideon's tribe, where he says his family is poor

fleece.meaning: sheep's wool Gideon left out overnight, asking for a sign

notes: 'A winepress is a pit for treading grapes' is general background, not stated in the text. Confirm it is acceptable as written.
'Raiders sweeping in when the crops come up' paraphrases Judges 6:3–4.
Two readings of the greeting (God seeing what Gideon will become; a name he grows into because God goes with him) are offered without ranking.
Original: גִּבּוֹר הֶחָיִל (Judges 6:12). Confirm pointing and pronunciation.
